title: Write a git-history file into the planner and critic snapshot
summary: The planner and critic get a generated history file in their read-only snapshot. It holds the last 200 base commits (subject, date, changed paths), without records/ or private paths, and comes from plain git log at snapshot time. Both briefs name the file and say what it holds. No git repository goes in the snapshot, no history is rewritten, and the grants stay unwidened. The audience is the planner and critic agents, and the maintainer who judges whether they stop planning less often.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for the file, the briefs and the grants, plus a clean cargo test and clippy.
The snapshot time added is measured and recorded, citing job 20261024-115923-02gf.
Criteria check the file's contents and the brief text, not just that the code exists.
The history file excludes records/ and private paths.
One focused change across the listed files.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The history file lives at a fixed path in the snapshot root, such as HISTORY.txt; the producer picks the name and the briefs cite the same constant.
Private paths are excluded with the same filter the snapshot already uses for its file copy.
Commits whose changed paths are all excluded are omitted or listed without paths; the producer picks one and documents it.
The 200 commits are counted on the base commit after exclusion, not before.
The earlier proposals (git log/show/diff grants, budgets command grant) are dropped per the user's reply. The budgets printout is out of scope.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test in athena-git builds a planning snapshot of a fixture repository with several commits, including one touching records/ and one touching a private path. It checks that the history file exists with one entry per commit (subject, date, changed paths), is capped at 200 commits, and contains no records/ or private path. Run: cargo test -p athena-git snapshot.
The snapshot contains no .git directory and the user's repository is unchanged by snapshotting. A test checks this. Run: cargo test -p athena-git snapshot.

A briefs test shows planner_brief and critic_brief each name the history file's path and say what it holds (last 200 commits, subject, date, changed paths, records/ and private excluded) and that Read and Grep are used on it. Run: cargo test -p athena-context briefs.
A test in athena-core asserts the planner and critic grants are unchanged: no Bash or git commands, writes false. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
The time the history file adds to snapshotting is measured, and the figure (labeled as a measurement, with the repository and method) is recorded in docs/decisions.md.

CHANGELOG.md has an entry, and docs/decisions.md records the decision. It lists the alternatives (git repository in the snapshot, widened git grants, plain copy), the choice, and cites job 20261024-115923-02gf.
cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check all pass.

out_of_scope: Giving the planner or critic Bash or git command grants
Putting a .git directory or any repository in the snapshot
Providing the budgets test output to the planner and critic
Changing the producer or verifier snapshots
urgent_reason: Giving the planner and critic the history cuts planning stops and post-plan rejections that came from facts only history shows, such as the broken land on every pull request in job 20261024-115923-02gf.
